query: I just moved to Tampere from the US on a 1-year work visa. Am I entitled to use the public healthcare system, and what is the cost?
expected_answer: If you register a municipality of residence (kotikunta) with DVV in Finland, you are entitled to use public healthcare services. Since you hold a work permit valid for at least one year, you are eligible to register. Once registered, you will pay the exact same local patient fees as permanent residents of Finland.

query: I am visiting Finland as a tourist from Canada. If I get sick or have an accident, can I go to a public hospital, and who pays for it?
expected_answer: In an emergency, you have a right to receive urgent medical care in the Finnish public healthcare system regardless of your nationality. However, if you do not have a municipality of residence in Finland or an EHIC card, you will be billed for the full, actual cost of your treatment. You should ensure you have private travel insurance to cover these costs.

query: I am a Spanish citizen studying at Aalto University for 6 months. How do I prove that I am entitled to medical care in the public system?
expected_answer: As an EU citizen, you can prove your right to medically necessary care in public clinics by presenting your valid European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) issued by Spain. This card entitles you to receive medically necessary treatment in the public healthcare system for the same patient fee as local residents.

query: I am a student from India applying for my first study permit. Do I need to buy private health insurance, and what does it need to cover?
expected_answer: Yes, non-EU/EEA students must have private health insurance. If your degree studies in Finland last for two years or more, your insurance must cover medical expenses up to at least EUR 40,000. If your studies last for less than two years, the insurance must cover medical expenses up to at least EUR 120,000.

query: I have a sudden, severe toothache. Can I go to a public health center for dental treatment, and how long is the waiting time?
expected_answer: Yes. If you have a municipality of residence in Finland, you are eligible for public dental care. In an emergency (such as severe pain, bleeding, swelling, or trauma), you can contact the urgent dental care clinic in your wellbeing services county for same-day treatment. For non-urgent dental care, there is usually a waiting list that can last several months.

query: I have a foreign prescription from my doctor in Germany. Can I buy my prescription medicine at a Finnish pharmacy?
expected_answer: Yes, you can buy prescription medicine if the prescription is a European prescription written by a healthcare professional in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland. You must present the paper prescription and your passport or official identity card at the Finnish pharmacy. Narcotic drugs or certain strong medications cannot be dispensed using a foreign prescription.
